bottom_line: Stocks had a rough day even though Anthropic, the company that makes Claude, had a huge stock market debut. The bigger story is the Fed (the people who set interest rates): inflation is still too high, and Fed officials are openly talking about raising rates again, which makes borrowing more expensive for everyone.

stories.title: Big AI debut, market still falls
stories.real: Anthropic started trading on the Nasdaq, jumped 27% and was valued at about $1.8 trillion. The wider market dropped anyway: the Dow sank 1,084 points, the Nasdaq fell 2.2%, and the S&P 500 is on its longest losing streak since June. Investors wanted proof the AI boom was safe, and one big debut didn't give them that.

stories.title: The Fed wants higher rates
stories.real: Fed officials say inflation is too high. Goolsbee says it is 'way higher' than their 2% goal, and he won't rule out bigger rate increases. The Fed's own meeting notes point to higher rates in December, and J.P. Morgan expects hikes at the next three meetings. Fed chair Kevin Warsh also has to figure out how a fast AI building boom affects jobs and prices.
stories.you: Higher rates usually mean pricier credit cards, car loans and mortgages, while savings accounts may pay a bit more.

stories.title: Nvidia under legal pressure
stories.real: California's attorney general, Rob Bonta, subpoenaed Nvidia (it sent a legal demand for records) in a probe into whether AI chips were diverted to China. This came right after CEO Jensen Huang left the company. Separately, AMD fell over 7% after a short seller (an investor who bets a stock will fall) claimed its firmware showed up at a blacklisted Chinese company. AMD says it follows U.S. law.
stories.you: Chip companies are a big part of many tech and index funds, so legal trouble at these firms can move your retirement account too.

stories.title: Gold drops, dollar gets stronger
stories.real: Gold slid to near $3,500 an ounce and is heading for its worst week in 8 months. When people expect higher U.S. interest rates, the dollar usually gets stronger, and gold tends to lose some of its appeal.
stories.you: If you bought gold as a safe place to park money, this is a reminder that it can fall too.

stories.you: Jobs look fairly steady for now, but everyday costs like fuel are still squeezing household budgets.
